beats.say: A penny gets you a whole music library. And the bill arrives later.
Sign up for a penny and receive twelve records.
Or pay the regular club price for a single album.
Or choose the no-commitment trial with no shipments.
Members who ignored the deadline got a full-price album shipped - Sounds like a trap.
The penny option locks you in; the next shipment is automatic unless you say no.
That hidden purchase drove $1.4 billion revenue in 1996, then collapsed to $17 million by 2014.
The company filed for bankruptcy in 2015, proving the model unsustainable.
Gym - free 1-day pass, then mandatory $30 monthly plan.
Café - free coffee, then auto-order a $5 pastry each week.
Streaming app - free month, then $12 monthly subscription. The mandatory upgrade feels cheap compared to the hidden recurring cost.
Watch for an automatic next step after a "free" offer. Follow for more.
